cards.text: Jesus has performed so many signs right in front of the people. Not a rumor in the group chat, friend. RIGHT in front of them.

cards.question: After all those signs right in front of them, the people believe in Jesus.

cards.text: Then the story reaches back to Isaiah the prophet, who asked, “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?” Friend, I've asked that first question after every joke I've ever told.

cards.question: The story says those words from Isaiah the prophet are fulfilled. Fulfilled by what?

answers.text: The people not believing in Jesus
The Greeks asking to see Jesus

cards.text: So they were unable to believe, and Isaiah has more to say: “He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts,” so they can't see with their eyes, understand with their hearts, or turn.

cards.question: In Isaiah's words, if the people could see, understand and turn, they would be healed.
The story says Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus' ___ and spoke about Him.

cards.text: Now HOLD ON, friend, because many of the LEADERS believe in Him! But believing it and saying it out loud? That's a whole other batch.

cards.question: The leaders who believe in Jesus confess Him out loud for everyone to hear.
Those believing leaders keep quiet because of the Pharisees, a strict Jewish religious group. What are the leaders afraid of?

answers.text: Being put out of the synagogue
Losing their seats at the feast

cards.question: The story tells why those leaders keep quiet. What do they love more than God's approval?

cards.text: Then Jesus cries out, and not a whisper or a mumble, friend. He CRIES OUT, and it's about believing in Him.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever believes in Him doesn't believe in Him alone. Who else do they believe in?
Jesus says whoever sees Him sees the One who sent Him.

cards.text: Then Jesus says He has come into the world as a light. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, so nobody has to explain to ME why that matters.

cards.question: Jesus came into the world as a light so that no one who believes in Him should remain in ___.

cards.text: Now Jesus talks about anyone who hears His words and doesn't keep them. That's hearing the oven timer go off and staying right there on the couch.

cards.question: Jesus says He judges anyone who hears His words and doesn't keep them.
Jesus says He did not come to judge the world. What did He come to do?

cards.text: But there IS a judge for the one who rejects Jesus and doesn't receive His words. And the judging comes on the last day.

cards.question: On the last day, what does Jesus say will judge the one who rejects Him?

cards.text: Jesus says He has not spoken on His own. Me? I speak on my own ALL day, and the dough has heard things it can't unhear.

cards.question: Jesus hasn't spoken on His own. Who has commanded Him what to say and how to say it?

cards.text: And Jesus knows the Father's command leads to eternal life.

cards.question: So Jesus speaks ___ what the Father has told Him to say.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of the scene: John's narration follows Jesus leaving and hiding Himself (John 12:36), and "they" are the crowd from that scene. The opening card doesn't say who is telling this, who "the people" are, or what has just happened. It only restates verse 37's signs.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke uses Isaiah's "Lord, who has believed our message?" as the line Papa Dorin says after his own jokes. The core action in the text is a message not being believed. A joke falling flat is about not getting a laugh, not about disbelief, so the comparison doesn't share the action. It also makes the Scripture quote itself the punchline.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: "But believing it and saying it out loud? That's a whole other batch" all but tells the baker that the leaders don't confess Him. That gives away the True/False answer on card 9.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The story card runs three sentences: "Now HOLD ON...!", "But believing it and saying it out loud?" and "That's a whole other batch."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Their own safety" can be argued as right. The card before it says the leaders keep quiet out of fear of being put out of the synagogue, so a baker could say they put their own safety ahead of God.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Of the stop's 9 choice cards, 5 are multiple choice, 2 are true or false and 2 are fill in the blank, including three multiple choice cards in a row (cards 8, 10, 12). Multiple choice dominates the stop.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "And Jesus knows the Father's command leads to eternal life." is a bare restatement of the verse with none of Papa Dorin's voice, on the last story card of the walkthrough.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
